gap:logistic_model_tuning.statement: Need to fit logistic regression models with specific conventions (full-batch GD, 200 iters, lr=0.1) and evaluate: (1) optimal L2 regularization, (2) value of interaction features, (3) compression tradeoffs via sparsity and quantization

hyp:l2_helps_cv.statement: L2 regularization should improve 5-fold CV Brier score over baseline lambda=0

hyp:interactions_improve.statement: Interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) may improve model performance, detectable via paired t-test

hyp:compression_tradeoff.statement: Compression via sparsity and quantization will degrade performance, with varying retention depending on sparsity level and bit width

claim:q1_best_lambda.statement: L2 regularization lambda=0.1 achieves the lowest 5-fold CV Brier score (0.207077) compared to lambda values [0.0, 0.01, 1.0, 10.0], with improvement of 0.0089 over baseline (lambda=0)

claim:q2_interactions.statement: Adding interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) significantly improves model performance. Paired t-test across 5 folds shows t-stat=3.912 (> 2.0), indicating interaction features help reduce Brier score

claim:q3_best_compression.statement: Among sparsity levels (20, 40, 60)% and bit widths (8, 4), the configuration sparsity20_bits4 retains the highest performance (retention=0.999222) with in-sample Brier score closest to dense model (0.141873 vs 0.141762)
